topic: Universal resampling-degeneracy certificates and power-optimal exact kernels for network exposure-effect quantiles. For a finite positive design law π on Ω and a directed legal-support relation L, let K be a row-stochastic kernel supported on L and define d_K(A) as the minimum over orderings σ of nonempty A of the maximum prefix mass K(σ_j,{σ_1,…,σ_j}). Prove that upper-tail p-values from K are super-uniform for every real score vector iff d_K(A)≥π(A) for every nonempty A; derive the peeling/core equivalence, O(|Ω|2^|Ω|) recursion and violated-subset certificate, exact union-of-polyhedra description, and a certified mixed-integer optimizer for power against a prespecified alternative catalogue. Within predeclared imputable network-exposure fibers, compute worst-case p-values over sharp schedules having at most r direct effects above c and invert the nested family into exact simultaneous lower bounds for exposure-specific effect quantiles. Credit Caughey–Dafoe–Li–Miratrix for bounded-null quantile RI, Owusu and Hoshino for network conditional tests, Zhang–Zhao for partition-sufficient conditional randomization, and Ramdas et al. for arbitrary-permutation constructions; use Owusu's Cai–de Janvry–Sadoulet weather-insurance reanalysis as the consumer. PRESOLVE EVIDENCE REQUIRING VERIFICATION: The score-blind presolve derived the universal-validity iff by ordering rejection sets and constructing a strict score order from every violating subset; it derived d_K(A)=min_i max{K(i,A),d_K(A\{i})}, the equivalent nonempty-core certificate, exact O(m2^m) separation, and a finite disjunctive MILP. It solved the uniform three-state cyclic nonpartition kernel and proved composite bounded-null validity using the supremum over null-consistent sharp schedules. Threshold equality, ties, zero-mass states, missing self-loops, outcome adaptation, tiny fibers, naive Monte Carlo, generic disjunctive collapse, and Ramdas et al. were checked; no collision was found. UNRESOLVED BOTTLENECK: For a fixed network rank statistic and legal exposure fiber, prove a terminating exact weak-order, LP, or MILP reduction of the worst-case composite-null p-value over schedules with at most r effects above c, including the simultaneous quantile-projection identity. EARLY KILL TEST: On one actual Cai/Owusu exposure fiber at α=0.05, compare the globally optimized kernel with every partition kernel and compute one bounded-null quantile p-value exactly; stop or pivot if legal support forces partitions, no strict certified power gain exists, or exact worst-case computation changes the target. open_problems.why_unsolved: Caughey et al. simplify the sharp-schedule supremum because their distribution-free statistic has an assignment-invariant tail law and the binary-treatment schedule has a separable order structure. Within a network-exposure fiber, changing one schedule coordinate can alter several assignment-specific ranks and rejection indicators, so that monotonicity argument no longer separates. Owusu obtains imputability by conditioning but does not give the required finite exact optimization. The prior endpoint/orbit construction has a fixed kernel and precomputed decision table; its first proof step must be replaced by joint enumeration of feasible schedules and induced score weak orders.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: An equality representing the composite-null p-value as a maximum over finitely many schedule and score-weak-order cells, with a terminating exact LP, MILP, or equivalent algorithm returning an optimizing sharp schedule and an auditable optimality certificate.

writing_exemplar.why: Its framing makes the sharp-schedule supremum the bridge from exact sharp-null inference to scientifically useful heterogeneous-effect conclusions.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: sharp-null randomization inference is exact but substantively narrow -> bounded nulls allow heterogeneous unit effects -> validity requires maximizing over compatible sharp schedules -> network exposure requires a new exact optimizer because ranks are coupled across assignments

method_exemplars.technique: Transform quantile-null p-value maximization into integer optimization and exploit a multiple-choice knapsack representation to obtain exact or certified-conservative solutions.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It is the nearest exact computational reduction for a cardinality-constrained sharp-schedule supremum; the network problem replaces separable stratum choices with fiber-coupled rank constraints.

method_exemplars.technique: Encode imputability as a unit-assignment graph and restrict randomization inference to a biclique on which the partially sharp null becomes sharp.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Its biclique construction supplies the finite legal assignment fiber on which every candidate schedule and rank comparison must be evaluated.

method_exemplars.technique: Condition on treatment functions to sharpen network heterogeneity nulls and control remaining nuisance parameters through maximization, splitting, or confidence-set restriction.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It confronts the same multiple-potential-outcome obstruction under network exposure, while the desired resolution replaces its partly asymptotic nuisance treatment with exact finite optimization.

open_problems.open_problem: Characterize exactly when the one-step upper-tail value p_K(x;s)=K(x,{y:s(y)≥s(x)}) is super-uniform under a finite positive design law for every real score vector, when K is supported by a directed legal relation.

open_problems.why_unsolved: Zhang–Zhao's sufficient construction is partition-based, while Ramdas et al. create exchangeable resamples using auxiliary randomization over transformations. Neither characterizes the unmodified, state-dependent tail mass generated by arbitrary rows K(x,·) under directed legality constraints. The missing necessity argument must work uniformly over score vectors by converting every violating subset into a strict score order whose rejection event has design mass above its nominal kernel tail mass.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A necessary-and-sufficient subset/order inequality for universal super-uniformity, together with an equivalent nonempty-core or peeling certificate, an O(|Ω|2^|Ω|) separation recursion, and a violated-subset witness.

writing_exemplar.why: Its motivation moves from partially sharp causal nulls to conditioning structures and isolates construction of the conditioning event as a methodological question.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: partially sharp causal nulls invalidate unrestricted resampling -> conditioning restores imputability and exactness -> partition conditioning is only one construction -> characterize all legal state-dependent kernels that are exact for every score

method_exemplars.technique: Construct exchangeable resamples from arbitrary permutation laws and prove p-value validity through rank symmetry.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It is the closest proof that nonuniform, non-group resampling can remain finite-sample exact, but its symmetrization must be replaced by a score-uniform row condition on K.

method_exemplars.technique: Represent conditional randomization tests by finite assignment-space partitions and prove validity conditional on the realized cell.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Partition kernels are the benchmark subclass that the desired characterization must contain while identifying additional nonpartition kernels.

open_problems.why_unsolved: Puelz et al. reduce imputability to biclique selection, while Yanagi–Sei optimize a power proxy whose normality and correlation simplifications need not hold exactly. Existing minimax permutation theory analyzes a fixed resampling construction rather than optimizing state-dependent rows. The prior CausalSmith construction gives a finite primal-dual saddle problem only when its observation kernel is fixed. Here K is itself the decision variable, and the active subset/order validity disjunct changes with K; an exact disjunctive valid-kernel representation is therefore required before power can be optimized without a surrogate.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: An exact union-of-polyhedra description of universally valid legal-support kernels and a terminating mixed-integer or equivalent optimizer returning the catalogue-optimal K, active validity disjuncts, achieved exact rejection probability, and a rational or numerical certificate of strict dominance over the partition-kernel benchmark.

writing_exemplar.why: It frames conditioning-set choice as a power problem and makes the limitations of proxy-based selection explicit.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: interference makes interesting nulls nonsharp -> bicliques restore exact testing -> admissible bicliques can have sharply different power -> replace heuristic biclique selection with certified optimization over every universally valid legal kernel

method_exemplars.technique: Encode null imputability in a bipartite unit-assignment graph and construct exact conditional tests from bicliques.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Its graph naturally generates the legal-support relation, and its biclique tests form the partition benchmark against which strict improvement must be certified.

method_exemplars.technique: Control permutation critical values and alternative rejection probabilities nonasymptotically through concentration and coupling arguments.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Its fixed-test power analysis supplies tools for bounding catalogue power once a candidate legal kernel has been selected.

method_exemplars.technique: Derive a power criterion for biclique randomization tests and use it to modify focal-unit and assignment-set selection.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It is the nearest optimization framework for power under interference, with its approximate criterion replaced by exact rejection probabilities and global certificates.

open_problems.why_unsolved: Caughey et al.'s simultaneous coverage follows from one nested family indexed by effect rank and threshold, and Su–Li retain that structure across disjoint randomized strata. Network exposures instead create overlapping imputable fibers and consistency restrictions on potential outcomes shared by several contrasts. Independently maximizing within each fiber or threshold may therefore select mutually incompatible schedules and need not equal projection of one joint confidence set. The prior finite-schedule construction varies one scalar functional and supplies no cross-threshold nesting or shared-schedule compatibility lemma.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: Either a finite-sample projection theorem giving an explicit jointly nested acceptance region whose inversion yields simultaneous one-sided lower bounds for all exposure-specific quantiles, or a finite counterexample and corrected compatibility constraints that restore simultaneous coverage.

writing_exemplar.why: Its framing explains why simultaneous quantile conclusions are a direct scientific payoff of bounded-null inversion rather than an ancillary multiplicity exercise.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: average effects conceal individual heterogeneity -> bounded-null tests reveal how many effects exceed each threshold -> nested inversion gives all effect quantiles simultaneously -> extend the projection identity to overlapping network-exposure contrasts

method_exemplars.technique: Invert a doubly nested family of exact bounded-null tests and prove simultaneous coverage for the ordered vector of individual treatment effects.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Its order-statistic projection is precisely the argument that must be generalized from one binary-treatment contrast to shared schedules across exposures.

method_exemplars.technique: Combine stratum-level integer optimizations while preserving simultaneous validity for all treatment-effect ranks.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It shows how exact quantile inversion can survive structured assignment restrictions, though not the overlapping fibers and cross-exposure consistency present here.

method_exemplars.technique: Define exposure-mapped potential outcomes and design probabilities for coherent direct and spillover causal contrasts.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Its exposure-indexed potential-outcome framework supplies the common target space in which joint schedule compatibility and quantile projection must be stated.

source_refs.excerpt: every assignment orbit in the positive support of the independent design is a dual best response

open_problems.why_unsolved: The interference literature operationalizes legal comparisons through focal-assignment subsets or bicliques, whereas arbitrary-permutation results obtain non-group exactness through a different symmetrizing construction. The scan found no graph-theoretic boundary describing when row-dependent kernels supported on an imputability relation must arise from conditioning cells. The prior complementary-slackness argument concerns best responses in a fixed finite game, not whether the valid-kernel faces generated by L coincide with the partition hull. The first new step is therefore a directed-cycle and subset-core analysis followed by separation from the partition-kernel power region.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A necessary-and-sufficient combinatorial criterion on L for partition exhaustiveness, an exact finite decision procedure, and, whenever the criterion fails, an explicit cyclic legal kernel plus a dual certificate of strict power separation for a specified alternative catalogue.

writing_exemplar.why: It turns exact-test feasibility under interference into a concrete graph problem and treats bicliques as the primitive admissible object.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: partial sharpness restricts legal assignment comparisons -> a unit-assignment graph records those comparisons -> bicliques generate exact conditional tests -> determine whether directed legality permits exact kernels beyond every biclique partition

method_exemplars.technique: Encode imputability through a bipartite null-exposure graph and use biclique decompositions to construct exact tests.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The desired boundary must characterize precisely when this biclique and partition architecture is exhaustive.

method_exemplars.technique: Prove exactness for arbitrary nonuniform transformation distributions by constructing an exchangeable augmented resample.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It provides the nearest nonpartition existence mechanism and identifies the symmetry ingredient that a directed-cycle construction must replace.

literature_map:
Caughey–Dafoe–Li–Miratrix (2023, JRSSB, arXiv:2101.09195) convert bounded sharp-schedule nulls into exact treatment-effect-quantile inference and simultaneous bands, while the general schedule supremum remains computationally difficult.
Su–Li (2024, Biometrika, arXiv:2208.11798) reduce exact quantile-null inference in stratified experiments to multiple-choice knapsack, providing the closest integer-optimization analogue.
Owusu (2023, arXiv:2308.00202) develops conditional randomization inference for heterogeneous effects under network exposure and reanalyzes the Cai–de Janvry–Sadoulet weather-insurance experiment; nuisance handling is partly asymptotic.
Hoshino–Yanagi (2026, Journal of Applied Econometrics, arXiv:2301.05580) test exposure-mapping specification through hierarchical conditional randomization and revisit the same insurance network.
Zhang–Zhao (2023, JASA, arXiv:2203.10980) formalize conditional randomization tests through assignment-space partitions and emphasize the design of conditioning events.
Ramdas–Barber–Candès–Tibshirani (2023, Sankhya A, arXiv:2204.13581) show that arbitrary nonuniform permutation laws can be exact after an exchangeability-restoring random modification.
Puelz–Basse–Feller–Toulis (2022, JRSSB, arXiv:1910.10862) encode imputability under general interference as a bipartite graph and construct exact tests from bicliques.
Yanagi–Sei (2022, arXiv:2203.10469) optimize biclique choice with an approximate power criterion, leaving room for exact globally certified optimization.
Athey–Eckles–Imbens (2018, JASA, arXiv:1506.02084) obtain exact p-values for nonsharp network-interference hypotheses through artificial experiments, anchoring the focal-assignment approach.
Basse–Feller–Toulis (2019, Biometrika) provide a general conditioning-mechanism framework for exact tests under interference.
Basse–Ding–Feller–Toulis (2024, Econometrica, arXiv:1904.02308) develop exact focal-unit randomization tests for peer effects in randomized group formation.
Aronow–Samii (2017, Annals of Applied Statistics, arXiv:1305.6156) supply the exposure-mapping estimand and design-probability framework; Hudgens–Halloran (2008, JASA) provide foundational direct and spillover finite-population estimands.
Kim–Balakrishnan–Wasserman (2022, Annals of Statistics, arXiv:2003.13208) give nonasymptotic minimax power tools for fixed permutation tests, complementary to legal-kernel optimization.
Cai–de Janvry–Sadoulet (2015, AEJ Applied, DOI:10.1257/app.20130442) is the live consumer: a directed friendship network, randomized information sessions, and economically meaningful insurance-adoption spillovers.
